---
title: Bank payouts
description: Add your bank once. The fee for that payout appears before you confirm.
---

You add your bank account once. When you pay out, the fee for that amount appears before you confirm.

## Add the account

Open Pay out. If there is no bank account yet, the screen asks you to add one and opens the bank form. You can also add it from Settings, then Payouts.

Enter the country of the bank, the name on the account, and the account number. A West African account is 24 characters and also needs the bank's SWIFT code. The account should be in the business name. You need a payout PIN first. Adding the account asks for that PIN.

The account is saved turned off. You cannot pay out to it until it is confirmed. A eurozone, UK, or Vietnam account is checked with the bank: a number that does not exist, or a name that is not the business, is refused. West African banks do not publish an account check, so a different name is still saved. The team gets an email to accept or refuse it. A number the bank says does not exist is refused.

Withdraw from the balance that matches the bank. A bank in Benin, Burkina Faso, Côte d'Ivoire, Guinea-Bissau, Mali, Niger, Senegal, or Togo pays F CFA. A eurozone bank pays euros. A US bank pays dollars. Convert first if the ledgers differ.

## What you pay

You receive the amount you enter. The fee is extra, and it comes out of the same balance.

The fee is two parts: the transfer cost, plus the lomi. share. The transfer cost is what the payout really costs to send: the exchange into the bank's currency and the bank network fee. The lomi. share is 0.5% of the amount plus 500 F CFA (1 EUR or 1 USD on euro and dollar payouts), and nothing else. The fee is calculated when you type the amount, and that exact fee is what you pay.

A local payout to one of those West African banks is in F CFA. The network fee on that local transfer is zero, so the transfer cost is the exchange into F CFA, about 1.3%. On 100,000 F CFA that is about 1,300 F CFA of transfer cost plus 1,000 F CFA for lomi., so a fee of about 2,300 F CFA. You still receive 100,000 F CFA. The balance goes down by about 102,300 F CFA.

A euro payout to a eurozone bank, or a dollar payout to a US bank, has no exchange and no network fee, so the fee is only the lomi. share. A bank the local networks do not reach is sent by international wire: the transfer cost is the 15 USD wire fee, plus the exchange if the currency changes.

It arrives in 1 to 5 business days. It is not instant.

Wave in Côte d'Ivoire is a separate payout, not this bank fee. A saved Wave number is 1%. A number you just added stays on a higher rate for 48 hours, then drops to 1%.

The payout screen shows what you receive, the transfer cost, the lomi. fee, and the total taken from the balance. Confirm only after the fee is on screen. If the fee cannot be calculated, the screen says so and you cannot confirm until it loads.

Through the API, the first `POST /payouts` call without `confirmation_token` returns `transfer_cost_amount`, `lomi_fee_amount`, `fee_amount`, and `total_deduction` for a bank payout. The payout you confirm with the token is priced the same way, at the rate of that moment, and takes exactly that total from the balance.
